It is found that a minimum inter-val of 1\musmust be allowed for reliable identification of bits at the receiving end. If the allowable voice bandwidth for telephone line transmission is 3kHz and the quantization level is given as 16, approximate the number of voice signals that can be multiplexed.

Options: 
A. 45 signals
B. 90 signals
C. 80 signals
D. 50 signals
E. 150 signals
F. 100 signals
G. 30 signals
H. 75 signals
I. 120 signals
J. 60 signals

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

For one voice signal with a bandwidth of $3 \text{ kHz}$, the Nyquist sampling theorem dictates a sampling rate of at least $2 \times 3000 = 6000 \text{ samples/sec}$. The quantization levels are 16, which requires $\log_2(16) = 4$ bits per sample. The bit rate per signal is therefore $6000 \times 4 = 24,000 \text{ bits/sec}$.
The approximate number of signals $N$ that can be multiplexed is the total capacity divided by the rate per signal: $N = 1,000,000 / 24,000 \approx 41.66$.
Among the given options, 45 signals is the closest approximation to 41.66.
